articleTitle: Standardisation of scalable coding schemes HDTV
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Digital Terrestrial Television,
abstract: Scalable coding schemes for HDTV are being considered in order to provide for compatibility with lower resolution scanning formats and for graceful degradation of the picture quality in the presence of transmission errors. This paper describes some of the schemes considered within the Moving Picture Experts Group (MPEG) and discusses the advantages and disadvantages of the different schemes which may be classified as frequency scalable, spatial scalable and SNR scalable. The selection of scalable schemes for inclusion in the MPEG standard is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Digital Terrestrial Television,
abstract: The author reports on the past two years' OFDM field trial with emphasis on broadcasting in so-called UHF 'taboo' channels to rooftop antennas. To prevent interference the OFDM signal must be transmitted at very low power, typically 30 dB down on neighbouring PAL services, but measurements indicate that coverage from main stations similar to that of existing PAL services is possible. Other scenarios such as transmitting with high power to portable receivers are also under consideration, although in the UK these would require significant changes to the existing UHF frequency plan. OFDM can offer the flexibility to meet many diverse requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Present status and future plans of the HD-Divine project
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Digital Terrestrial Television,
abstract: The Scandinavian R&D project HD-Divine (Digital Video Narrow-band Emission) at the International Broadcasting Convention 1992 demonstrated a system for digital terrestrial HDTV for the first time in Europe. The direction for new systems has since changed completely in favour of (completely) digital systems. An improved and extended version of the HDTV codec is able to handle four standard definition TV signals as an alternative to one HDTV signal. Various service objectives are discussed, and hierarchical and reconfigurable technical solutions compared. Support for the European DVB project in search of a common standard is outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency planning for digital terrestrial television
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Digital Terrestrial Television,
abstract: The European Broadcasting Union (EBU) have established a specialist group to study the overall spectrum availability for digital television in Europe. This paper presents an outline of planning studies within the group, and examines some results in the context of integrated digital planning, i.e. using existing television channels. Some results of BBC studies into UK national single frequency networks (SFNs), assuming the use of clear channels are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Combined source and channel coding: future directions for terrestrial broadcasting
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Digital Terrestrial Television,
abstract: This presentation concentrates on the importance of interoperability and on the methods by which it may be achieved. It gives a brief history of the development of HDTV, the performance parameters by which TV systems may be rated, and the system choices that must be made to achieve the desired capabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hierarchical digital broadcasting of TV and HDTV-the system approach of the /sup H/DTV/sub T/ project
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Digital Terrestrial Television,
abstract: The organisation and work schedule of the project are presented in relation to the European DVB project as a whole. A 'strawman' specification of the system is tabulated, with block diagrams of the transmitter and two codecs. Reconfigurable transmission based on a combination of multilevel channel coding and multiresolution QAM, and a scaleable video source coding scheme are explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Error correcting coding for OFDM broadcasting over frequency selective channels
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Digital Terrestrial Television,
abstract: This paper describes the channel conditions under which digital OFDM-based broadcasting systems should operate. Error correcting codes are used to improve the transmission reliability. For further improving the performance of the codes, the receiver needs knowledge about the channel conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Digital Terrestrial Television,
abstract: A number of individual digital television research and development projects are well underway, at both national and international levels, and a major effort to co-ordinate these activities has been launched. This paper briefly touches on these projects, drawing from information provided at the Oct 1993 meetings of the ITU-Radiocommunications Sector in Geneva. It describes the collaborative European research and development, Standards activities, including those of the EBU, ETSI and the ITU-R Sector, the HDTV Action Plan and MPEG developments. It concludes with a brief summary of the European DVB Project to provide overall co-ordination.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: COFDM for digital terrestrial networks: the right power at the right place
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Digital Terrestrial Television,
abstract: The performance of coded orthogonal frequency division multiplexing is considered from the aspects of impairments introduced by natural and artificial echoes and frequency planning. It is shown to offer an elegant solution to spectrum resource deficiency, and the power to render future terrestrial networks economic.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
